name: Dystopian Rebellion
definition: A character living under a totalizing harmful order learns how control operates and chooses resistance whose scale may range from private integrity to systemic change.
negative_signals: acute disaster before stable oppression forms
hidden conspiracy inside an otherwise ordinary society
diagnostic_questions: Does the world embody a sustained system of control?
Does resistance reveal both mechanisms and limits of that system?

neighbors.distinction: Dystopia openly structures everyday life through oppressive order.
Dystopia expands a designed social world; disaster reduces a familiar world through crisis.

reader_promises.name: System logic
reader_promises.description: Show how ideology, institutions, incentives, and daily routines reproduce oppression.

reader_promises.name: Resistance cost
reader_promises.description: Make every act of refusal alter safety, identity, solidarity, or possibility.

roles.name: Conditioned citizen
roles.description: Knows how to survive inside the system before learning to resist it.

roles.name: Resistance link
roles.description: Reveals alternatives while carrying a strategy, compromise, or risk.

roles.name: System agent
roles.description: Enforces control through belief, career, fear, or constrained duty.

stakes: Continuation or transformation of the regime
settings: Institution controlling reproduction, labor, or information

movements.name: Normalized control
movements.description: Dramatize ordinary participation in the system before exposing its contradiction.

movements.name: Breach of belief
movements.description: Make an experience or fact invalidate the protagonist's survival narrative.

movements.name: Resistance practice
movements.description: Move from private doubt to action while testing trust and strategy.

movements.name: System response
movements.description: Resolve how resistance changes the person, public, or institution even without total victory.

complications.name: Compromised resistance
complications.description: The opposition reproduces a coercive method or contains conflicting objectives.

complications.name: Loved enforcer
complications.description: Someone intimate benefits from or administers the system.

complications.name: Unequal freedom
complications.description: A proposed victory liberates one group by shifting cost to another.

twists.name: Managed rebellion
twists.description: The regime tolerates or shapes limited dissent to identify threats or renew legitimacy.

twists.name: System dependence
twists.description: Removing control immediately threatens a real service the society must replace.

conclusions.name: System overcome
conclusions.description: Collective resistance dismantles central mechanisms and accepts difficult reconstruction.

conclusions.name: Meaningful resistance
conclusions.description: The regime remains, but an act preserves values, people, or future possibility.

conclusions.name: Cautionary defeat
conclusions.description: Control absorbs the protagonist while the narrative clarifies how the outcome might have been prevented.

variation_axes.question: What scale of resistance is possible?

subversions: Give the system real internal disagreement and logistical limits.
Make building an alternative institution more important than destroying a symbol.
cliches_to_avoid: A regime that is cruel without functional mechanisms
A chosen rebel who replaces collective resistance
quality_checks: Control operates through specific daily practices.
Resistance requires coordination and creates consequences.
The ending identifies the scale and limits of change.

sources.title: The Five Types of Dystopian Narrative
sources.contribution: Distinguishes preventable dystopia, victorious resistance, conditional defeat, and other outcome patterns.

sources.title: Not Death, but Annihilation
sources.author_or_organization: University of Washington Department of English
sources.contribution: Describes dystopia as expansive world-building around extrapolated systemic disaster.
